title_x: Pricey for a productivity-based laptop. Also, NOT a touchscreen.
text:
Keep in mind that if you want a battery efficient laptop, one with an AMD 5000 series or an Intel 12th gen CPU will be best. I can't really justify this laptop's price margin with regards to the specs sheet. An Intel 11800h isn't the fastest laptop CPU, but it's still pretty fast for most people's use-cases.

For gaming, I would NOT recommend this laptop unless you're fine with 60hz and the graphical performance of a mobile Nvidia GTX 16 GPU w/ ray-tracing and DLSS. This can technically double as both a gaming laptop and a productivity machine, but it's mainly the latter. If you want one that's geared towards gaming, you could find one for much cheaper and with better specs. To put it into perspective, I bought a Lenovo Legion 5 Pro for $1400, and it had an AMD Ryzen 7 5800H processor (which is about equivalent to Intel's 11th gen mobile processor), a 140w Nvidia RTX 3070 mobile GPU, and a 165hz 1440p IPS display w/ HDR 400.

The display panel on the FusionTech ABC is definitely IPS. I could initially tell just from the viewing angles as there was little to no color shifting when I moved the screen around. This makes it decent for light photo or video editing as the color accuracy on IPS displays is phenomenal. The contrast isn't too bad, but it's not the best. It does not have HDR, which is pretty disappointing given the price point. The webcam quality is awful, but at least you get Windows Hello facial recognition.

The power button doubles as a fingerprint reader, but I personally don't like the location of it being in the upper right corner of the keyboard. I would have greatly preferred the power button being outside of the keyboard. However, I really liked the huge trackpad since it's a lot more ergonomic than most other laptops. The material quality feels very premium. The chassis appears to be brushed aluminum while the interior is carbon fiber.

I'd also like to mention that I was expecting this to come with a touchscreen, but that's apparently limited to the version of this laptop that has 4k resolution. Aside from that misnomer in the original product listing, I would recommend this laptop if it's within your price range. Otherwise, there are much cheaper laptops out there with similar or better performance and specs.

title_x: Terrible trackpad, battery life, and temperature control
text:
As others have mentioned, the trackpad is atrocious and this computer has some serious temperature control issues. I actually bought this computer specifically for its large trackpad. Having used various MacBooks as my personal computer for the last decade plus, I’ve gotten very used to never carrying around a mouse and keyboard with me, due to the MacBook’s fantastic trackpad. So, when I was told I’d need a Windows laptop for work, I chose this one specifically for its large trackpad. Unfortunately, the trackpad is completely unusable. Unlike others, mine actually has no wobble to it, but it is incredibly erratic and inconsistent in response. The mouse hiccups and stutters all over the place when using the trackpad, whereas it’s super smooth when using a mouse. Luckily, I use a dock with mouse and keyboard most of the time when I’m in my office at work.

Hilariously, the FusionTech dock I purchased with it doesn’t actually work correctly, as I get a warning every single time the computer boots up telling me the dock it’s plugged into is not to correct spec to provide full power and functionality, despite it being the dock FusionTech sells for this very computer (the highest watt one). It works fine, honestly, but I get hit with the error constantly because this computer is ALWAYS shutting down due to low battery power overnight, despite putting it into hibernate (not sleep) mode every night before I put it in my bag. The battery life in general is not great, but the fact that neither sleep nor hibernate mode will prevent it from dying overnight is unacceptable.

Perhaps worst of all, for most people anyway, this thing has really serious temperature control problems. It frequently sounds like a jet engine (PS4 Pro owners will know the sound well) while performing pretty simple tasks (like using Microsoft Office apps or browsing the web) and more intensive tasks require messing around with the power and fan settings to avoid the computer suddenly going black from overheating, something I experienced many times when I tried to play Civ 6 on it.

I truly cannot believe that this laptop costs what it does and has the reviews it does, because it is borderline unusable for many applications. Unfortunately, I cannot afford to be without a work computer for long enough to have it looked at, so I’m stuck with this thing until it drives me crazy enough to buy something else.

Two stars (instead of just one) simply because it does have a really nice screen.

I've owned lots of low and mid-range setups throughout my PC gaming life. Solid workhorses that would run all games but only at minimal framerates obtained by compromising that "ooh and ahh" factor. I wasn't totally cheaping out on budget rigs but I also wasn't aiming high. These were mediocre computers.

I finally aimed high with this laptop. A mobile RTX 3070 running on high wattage in a low profile chassis with a wonderful CPU. A sleek and solid build with a plethora of ports and dizzying array of customizatio options. The only slight drawback on my model is the soldered 16 GB of RAM, but I'm not a multitasker at all and I don't do high end video and 3D editing. RAM has never been a bottleneck for me.

I purchased this computer exclusively for gaming.

Specifically, I purchased it to hook up to a 34" ultrawide at 144hz to utilize GSync. And it works perfectly.

Games run sinfully smooth. I'm talking Warhammer II, Red Dead Redemption II, Star Wars Battlefront II, Dying Light, Dragon Quest XI, No Man's Sky, you name it.

The thermal profiles in the Advance Command Center also let me run the computer in different modes depending on whether I'm gaming or just watching videos. Cool mode runs low and quiet while Performance mode kicks up the fan level for that added oomph. This unit is also capable of overclocking and undervolting but I haven't used those options yet, as my system is working just fine and at manageable temperatures.

Overall this is a classy and well-engineered piece of technology that says, "I want a top 1% experience." This is a luxury laptop, an investment, impressive from all angles and one that I'm proud to say has finally broken me of my complacency with mediocre setups.

Game on, friends.

Long Review.
Gaming
I gave this for my son to play his game. His feedback is that it is acceptable for playing games while we are traveling. but he would prefer a better display and did say it is a little choppy compared to his Nvidia 3070. this is probably because the GPU memory is only half in Nvidia 3050 model.

Office/Regular use.

title_x: Very solid machine that can replace your desktop.
text:
There is a lot to like here from FusionTech. This laptop isn't inexpensive but it really shouldn't be. You get a really solid component spec sheet here. A powerful newest I7 processor, the newest (and highly sought after) Nvidia 3050 graphics card, 16gb of RAM, a 1tb solid state hard drive, an infrared facial recognition camera, a power button fingerprint scanner, and more. All of this is attached to a big 17" FHD screen. This screen is worth noting here as it isn't the best screen you can get from FusionTech on this laptop but it is a bright (500 nit) vibrant screen with tiny bezels. The trade off here is you get almost double the battery life at just over 9.5 hours of use. That is perfect for me and I don't miss the extra pixels. It is also worth noting that you don't have a touch screen here. Again, I don't mind that as I hate the fingerprints, but some might miss it. I have been using this for work for two weeks now. This laptop is fast. Really fast! It is able to handle robust graphics. All really good. It really is a joy to use. For me, there are a couple of things that stand out for me. First, this laptop knows when you open it so it is booting up as you do so. Combined with facial recognition, I am usually working almost as soon as I can get it open. Love this! I also love the build quality here. It is a real pleasure to work with. The carbon fiber platform is great and houses a really big touch pad. The keyboard build quality is also outstanding. All of this is housed in a full aluminum chassis. As I said, it is expensive but it earns the price tag. Lastly, while this is a 17" laptop, by slimming the bezels down, this laptop is actually the same size or smaller than a good percentage of 15.4" laptops on the market. I included a picture with my wife's 15.4" HP laying on top of it. FusionTech has been very efficient with their use of space here.

While great, this isn't perfect, and at $2,000, I feel like it should be or close. I love the inclusion of four high speed Thunderbolt ports. The laptop can charge through any of them and transfers are really fast. That said, there are exactly zero traditional USB-A ports or any other port for that matter. They do include a dongle to convert but still this seems like an oversight to me. I actually use the function keys for work. If you need to here, you will need to hit a function key to use them. Not a deal breaker but not convenient. In spite of it's slimmed down size, this laptop is also quite heavy. My work backpack isn't happy with me since this acquisition. Battery life is okay here for me but, even with the less impressive screen, you will need to have a battery back up handy for travel.

FusionTech has made a heck of a laptop here overall. It can handle gaming and probably almost anything you can throw at it for work. The speakers here are good (not groundbreaking but solid) and the web cam really makes a Zoom meeting look good. I am still working on Windows 11 but it is here. For $2,000, you are paying a premium but you are getting a premium experience in almost every way.

Well done FusionTech.

text:
I won't go into detail about all the features of this laptop. Those are available in the product description. It's a big, loaded, high-performing machine with several things I DO think are worth mentioning.

The first thing is that I got to experience FusionTech ProSupport because the main board failed about two weeks after receiving the laptop. I didn't really "dock" this product for that, because I felt experiencing support was a good review point and FusionTech's support was excellent. I spent less than five minutes in a chat explaining the issue (various blue screens) and FusionTech dispatched a shipping box, repaired unit and returned, all in a matter of a few days. The laptop has run without issue since.

What I like- I use this is in my den for all manner of internet searches and basic tasks. I like the touchscreen because it's handy to point and touch when this behemoth is sitting on my lap (never had it feel hot or even warm btw). Setup is straightforward with a guided tour of settings. Performance is very nice. There is no lag in anything I've ever tried to do with this device.

What I don't like- While I like the touchscreen, the actual screen is WAY oversaturated for my taste. I spent a considerable amount of time trying to find a balance that works for me. I'm not crazy about Windows 10 Pro and perhaps some of the bloat that gets installed (previous machines have been Windows Enterprise editions). I can't seem to find a good balance for power settings (only a few available), and there are lot's of pop-ups from FusionTech apps that required digging around to try and disable. Also, like a few others have mentioned, while I appreciate the aesthetics of only TB3 ports (and an SD reader), I'd like to have some older ports available that wouldn't require me to adapt because then the aesthetics are completely spoiled.

So, is it a buy recommendation? If you want a "bragging rights" machine that looks as good as it can perform- shaming even most desktops that aren't loaded out, and you aren't a big gamer, then YES, it's a nice package. I will say that I also have an Worktop 16 7610 with the same processor, memory, GPU, and hard drive. It's a slightly smaller screen with no touch, has a full compliment of ports, isn't anywhere near as pretty, and costs about $1,000 less.

Stable trackpad on mine (not that I ever use the trackpad, I am strictly speaking a mouse user in anything but an emergency and with a touch screen I would have to stretch to find just such an emergency). The specs on this laptop, while not top of the line, are certainly respectable, with room upgrading (disk and memory) to keep it performing well as it ages for a few years to come.

I tend to use this laptop for entertainment and gaming purposes and the graphics (GeForce RTX) and speed were of importance to me. I am not by any means a hardcore gamer or even competitive, but I do like to enjoy myself and that means reasonable response / FPS and minimal lag, all of which are achieved by this laptop. The touch screen is a nice feature, but mostly I plug this into a docking station (intpw thunderbolt dock) with a KVM switch and a Samsung 43" 4K TV as my monitor, so mostly it is the functional guts of the laptop that I am impressed by.

When I do go mobile, the 17" screen offers nice clear graphics (albeit scaled down from 43") that are adequate for most of the MMOs that I tend to play.

You will want to invest in a cooling pad or at the least a passive base to allow adequate circulation of air to cool this laptop, when running anything intensive it will heat up a little (and heat is death for processors).

I have not updated this laptop to Windows 11 yet, but the check shows it as ready (including the dreaded TPM issues) if you insist on living on the bleeding edge.

Overall, this has been a great upgrade for my older dinosaur of a laptop. P-)

text:
Tengo pocos días de estar usando esta laptop para trabajo, estudios y juegos. i7 11800H, RTX 3060, 16GB RAM dual channel, 512GB almacenamiento. La recibí sellada de fabrica.
Para trabajo y estudio es mas que excelente y sobrado, si te importa el peso, esta no es para ti, yo con todo gusto cargo esta laptop valorando sus capacidades. Si quieres una laptop que te dure la batería todo el día, búscate una laptop no gamer.
Para juegos es una maquina que no esperaba que fuera tan potente, y no esperaba que viniera con una RTX 3060 de 130w, ... feliz! La calidad de pantalla y el brillo es excelente aunque sea de 250 nits, son suficientes para que te duelan los ojos de la intensidad del brillo. Uso el brillo en 50% y es mas intenso que una laptop de bajo precio con brillo al maximo.
Es el equipo mas económico con Hybrid/Optimus (switch MUX), y es una gran ventaja para sacar todo el potencial de la RTX 3060 (15-20 fps adicionales con Optimus en Off), esta característica era importante para mi porque puedo tener toda la potencia de la gpu en la pantalla del mismo equipo y no depender de una pantalla externa para saber su verdadera capacidad.
La batería en optimus para ofimática y vídeos dura aproximadamente 3 horas y 45 minutos.
La refrigeración me parece muy funcional y muy silenciosa, con 4 salidas (2 laterales y 2 traseras) y 2 entradas amplias (por la parte de abajo y la parte superior, entre el teclado y la pantalla), recomiendo utilizar una muy buena base de refrigeración adicional para darle vida en el tiempo y cuidar tu inversión.
La tecla G activa la máxima velocidad de los ventiladores (para nada molestos) así como el brillo pero aun no he verificado si las frecuencias de la cpu o gpu suben, pero sin activar la tecla G es lo suficientemente potente para correr tus juegos en máxima calidad sin contratiempos.
Sobre el acabado, es de plástico, pero en mi opinión personal es plástico de muy buena calidad, excelente ensamble, muy solida por todos lados, fuerte, resistente y muy buen acabado. No es una laptop con diseño excesivo gamer, pero es diferente a una laptop común, discreta pero con un toque especial, sobrio y elegante.
Viene con Windows 11 para inicializar, que me parece mucho mejor que con windows 10 actualizable y tener problemas de drivers luego.

En resumen, encontré todas las características que buscaba por el dinero que pensaba invertir, hasta el momento cero fallas, gran potencia para juegos actuales. Si falla, actualizare este comentario.

text:
The FusionTech G5 15 is a step up from my previous laptop, and it works well for both business and personal use. It runs games as recent as Resident Evil: Village with only a few decreases in video quality needed. Its memory is divided up into 100 GB SD and 900 GB HD - programs and files on the SD will load quicker, so it is best to store most of your data on the HD if you don't mind it taking longer to load. Its battery life is strong as well.

My only complaint is that its fans are noisy, especially when you are playing a demanding game. It can also heat up fairly quickly, so I would recommend getting a cooling pad to go with it.

Overall, the pros of the laptop outweigh its cons. I wanted a higher-end gaming laptop without going over budget, and this model delivered on what I had hoped for. I purchased my model in December 2018, and it is still going strong as of writing. I would recommend it to people who want a compact, portable, and powerful gaming machine that can still work well with everyday applications.

title_x: Great Laptop if the Touchpad Worked
text:
This review is for the FusionTech Worktop 16 7610 16 Inch Thin Laptop (Intel Core i7-11800H, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Graphics, Windows 10 Pro.

On paper, this was the best laptop that I could find for what I was looking for: 16" monitor, 16 GB RAM, minimum 512GB NVMe SSD, Thunderbolt, 10 key pad, and backlit keyboard. I was strongly leaning towards Windows 10 Pro (for various reasons), which this also happened to have.

I don't do any gaming, so even the on-die GPU would have been sufficient, however I do like having the RTX 3050 if I were ever to hook up to external displays for an overall two or three display setup (including the laptop's monitor). The 16" monitor is a big step up in screen area compared to the 15.6" monitor that I had been using for years. I also like that this monitor has no glare and an amazing 3072 x 1920 pixel resolution. The screen looked really good. I was ok with the screen only getting 300 nits bright, but I wouldn't want to consider anything lower.

This laptop was surprisingly small and light, especially given the monitor size. It was actually smaller in length, width, height, and weight than my 15.6" laptop, and that's even with this FusionTech's battery being double the capacity of my old laptop.

The physical sliding webcam shutter was a nice bonus, and I wish all laptops had a physical shutter or physical switch to shut off webcam.

The keyboard and touchpad both felt pretty good. The keys had decent feedback (for a laptop) and the touchpad is the largest that I have seen on a laptop. Unfortunately, the touchpad is where everything fell apart for this laptop. The touch pad gets jittery and stops responding. I originally purchased an open box from a local retail store that had this touchpad problem show up within just minutes of usage. The IT center at the store also had it show up for them within a few minutes as well. They did a full driver update, and it worked for about 20 minutes, turned off the laptop, and the next day about five minutes in and the touchpad started having the same issues again. I then tried the brand new floor model (running Windows 11 Home), and a couple minutes of using the trackpad had the issue on that one too. Even the manager came over and had the same issue. He said he has seen the issue before, and he said FusionTech's answer was to replace the motherboard (including the soldered on CPU). I found many reviews, posts, forums, even video posts, and tech channels all talking about the dreaded touchpad issue that plagues this laptop. The tech channels showed three solutions: change graphic hardware settings, place filler material between the battery and touchpad, or to solder on a grounding wire (voids warranty). Ultimately, it was the touchpad issues that had me decide to return the laptop and look for something else.

Well, after you plug in the head set and remove it a couple times, it stops recognizing it all together. Solution: a F&**$&ng reboot.
